extracted.intended_audience: epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors involved in observational studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on how to report observational (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) epidemiological research using the STROBE Statement checklists; intended to improve completeness and transparency of reporting rather than to prescribe study design or judge study quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report what was planned (and what was not)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what was planned (and what was not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the pre-specified study plan, including any deviations from planned analyses or protocol elements; transparency about planning helps readers assess strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report what was done (complete methods description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what was done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail on study design, participants, exposures, outcomes, measurements, data collection, and analysis procedures so that readers can understand and potentially reproduce the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report what was found (complete results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results clearly and completely, including estimates, precision (e.g. confidence intervals), sample sizes, numbers included/excluded, and relevant subgroup or sensitivity analyses to allow assessment of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report what the results mean (interpretation and context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers need to know what the results mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings in context, discussing plausibility, limitations, potential biases, generalisability, and implications for practice or further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use STROBE checklist items appropriate to study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a checklist of items that should be included in articles reporting observational research, initially restricted to cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the STROBE checklist corresponding to their design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) or the combined checklist; STROBE also provides a checklist for conference abstracts. Checklists are available for download in PDF/Word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on reporting, not on design or conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations are not prescriptions for designing or conducting studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE focuses solely on improving the completeness and transparency of reporting; it does not dictate methodological choices or how studies should be run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist not an instrument to evaluate research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The checklist is not an instrument to evaluate the quality of observational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE aims to improve reporting clarity and completeness; absence or presence of checklist items should not be used as a direct measure of study validity or methodological quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope initially limited to main analytical designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational research comprises several study designs and many topic areas; STROBE initially restricts recommendations to the three main analytical designs used in observational research: cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions to other designs (e.g. nested case-control) and specific topic areas are anticipated and may be developed as separate extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE is an evolving initiative (updates, translations, extensions encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: The STROBE initiative should be seen as an ongoing process, with future revisions based on comments, critique and new evidence; translations and extensions are welcomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone intending to use STROBE for extensions, translations or related work is asked to contact the coordinating group first to coordinate efforts and avoid duplication; original authors hold copyright and materials are open-access on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal endorsement improves reporting uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations on the reporting of studies that are endorsed by leading medical journals can improve the quality of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek journal endorsement or follow journal policies that adopt STROBE to increase adherence and improve reporting standards across publications.
